what: Inside a full-screen panel, sections are laid out from right to left (scroll, vertical-writing book), and the whole panel is pushed right directly by the deltaY of the vertical wheel, bringing in the left sections. Arrows and PageUp/Down move 400px (page ×3) at a time over .4s ease-in-out, and a #link pointing to a section in the panel aligns that section’s right edge to the right edge of the screen over .4s ease-in-out. A finger drag follows as is, and on release it goes further by the last movement × 15 and stops in .3s (swing). It stops at the start and the end
ease: cubic-bezier(0.42,0,0.58,1) (key · link) · sine.inOut (after release, same formula as jQuery swing) · wheel has no curve, immediate

options.step: Distance (px) moved per key press, default 400
options.page: How many times step PageUp/Down moves, default 3
options.dur: Duration when moving by key·link (sec), default .4
options.fling: Multiplier applied to the last movement on release, default 15

use:
First section (far right)
Second Section
note: Since the part’s panel takes all wheel events (preventDefault), use the panel on a single-page layout that covers the screen height, and don’t combine it with document vertical scroll. Finger dragging is this part’s job, so the panel gets touch-action: none (outside the panel is not blocked). To move it from elsewhere, call the panel element’s fxTrackTo(position, length, curve), and it fires fx:move on every move. { pos, max } Fires it. Each section’s entrance effect is applied via IntersectionObserver, and the parts (strip-unroll etc.) pick up the transform as is

from.where: index.html .ng-stage (original main-min.js RtlScroller — wheel deltaY as is · velocity 1ms, keys 400px 400ms ease-in-out, anchors 400ms ease-in-out, touch accel ×15 → 300ms swing)
